valencia-30-wheels: Thirty centimetres of soil holds water like a small reservoir — wheeled 30s are the low-maintenance choice for sunny terraces.
capri-set-of-5: A staggered row of five pots at descending heights draws the eye down a wall or along a staircase naturally.
valencia-40-wheels: Valencia's wheeled base was designed for terrace gardeners — moving a heavy planter into shade takes seconds, not two people.
capri: Compact pots like CAPRI suit window sills and desk corners — where 90% of houseplants actually live.
capri-14-set-of-2-with-plant: A matched pair with plants included is the fastest way to style a shelf — no trial and error needed.
atlantis-set-of-3-with-plant: A trio of planters at three heights creates depth in a corner that a single pot never can.
valencia-25: A 25-cm planter suits most medium houseplants with room for a full year of growth.
valencia-20: Twenty centimetres is the classic windowsill size — deep enough for herbs, light enough to move daily.
valencia-16: Sixteen centimetres suits compact plants like succulents and small foliage — where overpotting is the real danger.
valencia-14: Smaller pots dry out faster — which is a feature, not a flaw, for plants that hate wet roots.
valencia-11: Tiny pots are where most plant kill happens from kindness — an 11-cm pot teaches you restraint with water.
bone-meal-manure: Bone meal releases phosphorus slowly over months — steady nutrition rather than a quick fix.
epsom-salt: A teaspoon of Epsom salt per month is the classic rose-grower trick for deeper green leaves.
verona-33-set-of-5-13-inch: A matched five-piece set at descending sizes creates a staircase of green — the layout professionals call a 'planter family'.
verona-22-set-of-5-8-6-inch: Grouped pots lose moisture slower than singles — a cluster shades its neighbours' soil and waters less often.
